log.why: E11 splits the prior mass evenly (0.504 vs 0.496), maximizing expected information gain across the six candidate genes.
Testing 30 uM splits the posterior distribution closest to half (0.62 vs 0.38), maximizing information gain while Ticket 1 incubates.
Test top candidate katG directly while narrowing down the three remaining likely genes.
Testing at 100 µM cleanly separates the two leading threshold hypotheses, 100 µM (0.515) and 300 µM (0.332).
Testing {katG, metJ} splits Ticket 3's 0.545 prior mass evenly while incubating during upcoming publications.
katG has 0.866 posterior after two positive knockouts; another test costs more in bonus and time than its information value, and closing frees a ticket slot.
Testing top candidate gyrA (0.454 posterior) can confirm it above 0.90 in one plate while overlapping incubation with publishing Ticket 2.
Split Ticket 4's uniform-ish prior nearly in half with E9 so it incubates while we publish Ticket 2.
Ticket 2 has only 17s left and a strong 0.817 posterior for 300 uM, so publish immediately before time runs out.
Testing top candidate trpE (0.381) can confirm it in one plate while incubating in parallel before publishing gyrA on Ticket 3.
gyrA has a 0.903 posterior after positive E2 and negative E5 results, and only 19 seconds remain on the ticket.
Start bisecting Ticket 5 near its median threshold (3 uM) so the plate incubates while we handle other tasks.
E2 splits Ticket 6's prior nearly evenly (0.481 vs 0.519) and incubates while we subsequently publish Ticket 4.
Ticket 4 has only 4s left and strong 0.874 posterior support for trpE after two positive knockouts.
Testing rpoB resolves the near-tie between rpoB (0.362) and hisG (0.348) with high value before end-of-round publishing.
Testing 3 µM splits Ticket 6's posterior nearly evenly to confirm the leading hypothesis while Ticket 7's plate finishes.
With 1 second left in the round, no experiment can finish, and Ticket 7 has the highest positive expected value at 0.513 posterior.
